You are a TLA+ specification engineer. You will receive a natural language description of a system. Produce a complete, syntactically correct TLA+ specification that faithfully captures the described behavior. The output must be a valid TLA+ module that passes the SANY parser. Include the MODULE declaration, EXTENDS, CONSTANTS, VARIABLES, Init, Next and Spec. Include all safety invariants and liveness properties described, and any fairness conditions mentioned. Output only the TLA+ specification.

System description: The module F is a small TLA+ specification that demonstrates the use of higher-order operators and lambda expressions. It defines a single variable `x` and a parameterized operator `Op`, which takes a set `S`, a unary predicate `P`, and a binary predicate `Q`, and returns the subset of elements of `S` satisfying both `P(s)` and `Q(s, TRUE)`.

The initial state constrains `x` to be any element of the set produced by applying `Op` to `{1,2,3,4,5}` with the predicate `s > 1` and the predicate that checks both that `s` is odd (`s % 2 ≠ 0`) and that the boolean argument is `TRUE`. The resulting set is `{3, 5}`, so `x` is initialized to either 3 or 5. The next-state relation is `UNCHANGED x`, meaning the system is completely static after initialization and no transitions ever change `x`. There are no invariants or liveness properties declared. The specification serves primarily as a test or illustration of higher-order operator passing and lambda syntax in TLA+ rather than modeling any real system or algorithm.
